title: Calorimetry: mixing and the balance of heat (ক্যালোরিমিতির মূলনীতি)
placement: Book pages 179-181, section 6.6 ক্যালোরিমিতির মূলনীতি (Fundamental Principles of Calorimetry): next to the two rules (i) and (ii) and the three worked examples (ice in 1 liter of 30°C water, 2 liter of 75°C water with 1 liter of 20°C water, a 10 gm piece of 120°C iron in 1 kg of 30°C water).
description: The principle of calorimetry (ক্যালোরিমিতির মূলনীতি, pages 179-181, 6.6) on a lab bench: a 3 litre glass beaker of water with a pen thermometer in it, and on the left what the book adds to it. Three examples as the row of words, exactly the book's: বরফ (a 100 gm piece of ice at 0°C let go in 1 liter of 30°C water; L = 334 kJ/kg; T = 20°C), দুই পানি (a mug of 1 liter at 20°C poured into 2 liter at 75°C; T = 56.6°C) and লোহা (a 10 gm piece of iron at 120°C, glowing, let go in 1 kg of 30°C water; s = 0.45 × 10³ and 4.2 × 10³; T = 30.1°C). One action, one result, one rule: the big numbered button adds the thing (the ice is lifted over the beaker and let go, floats and melts; the mug is tipped about its lip and the stream raises the level; the iron drops to the bottom, bubbles, and stops glowing) while the thermometer's screen follows the temperature of the mixture and the water's tint turns from warm to cool; the ring and the same badge on the thing to add show what to touch. The panel is in the lab's order: the readings are the book's givens (masses with m₁ and m₂ as the book's equation uses them, temperatures, specific heats, L), then the book's balance equation and T written out as the book does (and with the student's numbers once it ran), the heat given and taken (equal, about 41,800 J; 1,54,000 J; 405 J), and the book's two rules: (i) the hotter body keeps giving heat until the temperatures are equal, (ii) the hot body gives exactly as much as the cold body takes (nothing is lost). Test tab: 5 tap questions on frozen scenes (which way the heat goes, the final temperature of two waters with the usual wrong averages, the heat to melt 100 gm of ice, why a little hot iron barely warms 1 kg of water, the ice's whole heat m₁L + m₁sT). Phone-first, Bangla.
